selector.champion: Extranodal natural killer/T-cell lymphoma nasal type
selector.rationale: The punch biopsy showing a sparse perivascular and interstitial infiltrate of enlarged atypical mononuclear cells, along with elevated lactate dehydrogenase, mild lymphocytopenia, and systemic symptoms like intermittent fevers and night sweats, supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Leukemia
rejected.why: Lack of specific evidence in the vignette to strongly support this diagnosis over the champion.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Insufficient evidence in the vignette to support this diagnosis, especially with the presence of atypical mononuclear cells.

rejected.label: Pyomyositis
rejected.why: The patient did not improve with antibiotics, and the biopsy was not consistent with cellulitis or pyomyositis.

rejected.label: Histiocytosis
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and biopsy findings do not specifically support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: While lymphoma is a consideration, the specific findings and biopsy results more strongly support the champion diagnosis, which is a subtype of lymphoma.

support_spans: A punch biopsy of skin from the lower leg showed a sparse perivascular and interstitial infiltrate of enlarged atypical mononuclear cells in the reticular dermis and subcutis, not consistent with cellulitis.
intermittent fevers, episodic night sweats, decreased appetite, and palpitations
contradict_spans: He was started on intravenous ceftriaxone for presumed cellulitis and pyomyositis but did not improve.
CT and MRI of the leg revealed gastrocnemius myositis, extensive subcutaneous and superficial myofascial edema, and popliteal lymphadenopathy without evident lymphatic obstruction.
